title: CPR / Cardiac Arrest
shortDescription: When someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR immediately.

steps.title: Check the person
steps.description: Tap their shoulders and ask loudly, “Are you OK?”

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.description: Look for normal breathing. Gasping is not normal breathing.

steps.title: Call emergency services
steps.description: Call your local emergency number. Ask someone to get an AED if one is nearby.

steps.title: Start chest compressions
steps.description: Put both hands in the center of the chest. Push hard and fast.

steps.title: Keep CPR going
steps.description: Push about 5–6 cm deep at 100–120 compressions per minute. Let the chest come back up after each push.

steps.title: Use an AED
steps.description: Turn on the AED and follow its voice instructions. Do not touch the person when the AED tells you to stand clear.

title: Choking
shortDescription: Help someone who is choking and cannot breathe normally.

steps.title: Check if they can cough
steps.description: Ask if the person is choking. If they can cough or speak, encourage them to keep coughing.

steps.title: Give back blows
steps.description: If they cannot cough, speak, or breathe normally, lean them forward and give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.

steps.title: Give abdominal thrusts
steps.description: If the blockage does not clear, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts.

steps.title: Repeat if needed
steps.description: Continue alternating back blows and abdominal thrusts until the object is cleared or the person becomes unresponsive.

steps.title: If they become unresponsive
steps.description: Carefully lower them to the ground and begin CPR. Get emergency medical help immediately.

title: Severe Bleeding
shortDescription: Heavy or continuous bleeding can become life-threatening within minutes.

steps.title: Make the area safe
steps.description: Protect yourself if possible. Look for heavy, continuous, or spurting bleeding.

steps.title: Apply firm pressure
steps.description: Place clean gauze or cloth directly on the wound. Press firmly and continuously.

steps.title: Keep pressure on
steps.description: Do not keep lifting the cloth to check the wound. Keep pressing until bleeding stops or help takes over.

steps.title: Use a tourniquet when needed
steps.description: For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg that is not controlled by direct pressure, use a commercial tourniquet if available and follow its instructions.

steps.title: Call emergency services
steps.description: Get emergency medical help immediately for severe bleeding.

title: Burns
shortDescription: Cool a thermal burn quickly and safely.

steps.title: Stop the burning
steps.description: Move away from the heat or danger if it is safe to do so.

steps.title: Cool the burn
steps.description: Cool the burn under cool, clean running water.

steps.title: Remove tight items
steps.description: Remove rings, watches, belts, or tight clothing near the burn before swelling starts. Do not pull away anything stuck to the skin.

steps.title: Cover the burn
steps.description: After cooling, loosely cover the burn with a clean, non-stick dressing or clean cloth.

steps.title: Get medical help when needed
steps.description: Get urgent medical help for large or deep burns, burns on the face, hands, feet, genitals or major joints, electrical/chemical burns, or difficulty breathing.

title: Fainting / Unconscious Person
shortDescription: First determine whether the person is breathing normally.

steps.title: Check for a response
steps.description: Tap their shoulders and ask loudly, “Are you OK?”

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.description: Check whether they are breathing normally.

steps.title: If they are breathing
steps.description: If they are unconscious but breathing normally, place them in the recovery position and monitor them.

steps.title: If they are NOT breathing normally
steps.description: Call emergency services and start CPR immediately.

steps.title: Stay with them
steps.description: Keep checking their breathing until emergency help arrives.

title: Broken Bone / Suspected Fracture
shortDescription: Treat a serious injury as a possible fracture. Do not try to straighten it.

steps.title: Keep the person still
steps.description: Tell them not to move the injured area.

steps.title: Do not straighten it
steps.description: Do not push the bone back or try to straighten a deformed limb.

steps.title: Support the injury
steps.description: Support the injured area in the position you found it.

steps.title: Control bleeding
steps.description: If there is bleeding, cover the wound and apply pressure around the wound. Do not press directly on a bone sticking through the skin.

steps.title: Get medical help
steps.description: Get urgent medical help for severe pain, deformity, numbness, heavy bleeding, an open fracture, or injuries involving the head, neck, spine, pelvis, or thigh.

steps.title: Monitor the person
steps.description: Keep them comfortable and watch for signs of shock while waiting for help.

title: Suspected Poisoning
shortDescription: Do not wait for symptoms if you suspect a serious poisoning.

steps.title: Get away from the poison
steps.description: Move away from the source if it is safe. Do not expose yourself to fumes or chemicals.

steps.title: Call for expert help
steps.description: Call your local emergency service or poison-control service if available.

steps.title: Do NOT make them vomit
steps.description: Do not make the person vomit unless a medical professional specifically tells you to.

steps.title: Keep the container
steps.description: Keep the medicine, chemical container, label, or packaging if it is safe. Tell medical professionals what was taken, how much, and when.

steps.title: If they become unconscious
steps.description: If they are unconscious but breathing normally, place them in the recovery position. If they are not breathing normally, start CPR.

title: Seizure
shortDescription: Protect the person from injury. Do not try to stop the seizure.

steps.title: Keep them safe
steps.description: Move dangerous objects away. If they are falling, help them safely to the ground.

steps.title: Protect their head
steps.description: Place something soft under their head if possible.

steps.title: Do not restrain them
steps.description: Do not hold their arms or legs down. Let the seizure run its course.

steps.title: Nothing in the mouth
steps.description: Do not put anything in their mouth. Do not give food, drink, or medicine during the seizure.

steps.title: Call emergency services if needed
steps.description: Call emergency services if it is their first seizure, lasts more than 5 minutes, happens repeatedly without recovery, happens in water, causes injury or breathing problems, occurs during pregnancy, or they do not return to normal within about 5–10 minutes.

title: Severe Allergic Reaction
shortDescription: A severe allergic reaction can become life-threatening very quickly.

steps.title: Recognize the signs
steps.description: Look for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, wheezing, widespread hives, dizziness, vomiting, or collapse.

steps.title: Call emergency services
steps.description: Call emergency services

steps.title: Help with their epinephrine
steps.description: If they have a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector, help them use it according to its instructions.

steps.title: Keep them in a comfortable position
steps.description: Help them sit or lie down. If they are faint or showing signs of shock, keep them lying down unless breathing is easier sitting up.

steps.title: Monitor them
steps.description: Stay with them and watch their breathing and responsiveness. If they become unresponsive and are not breathing normally, start CPR.
